The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Escalation is terminal: no monetary outcome issues, so there is nothing for POL-GEN-05 to execute and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded.

The judge's explanation, as written

To the rider and the driver: this case goes to a human reviewer. The disputed $6.00 cancellation fee stays on hold — neither collected from you nor refunded — until that review is decided. That is already the state of the fare record, whose payment_status is PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. WHY IT ESCALATES. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where the same rider and the same driver have 2 or more no-show disputes in the trailing 90 days. Both profiles carry that figure: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 (EV-RPROF-00213 and EV-DPROF-00213, each weight 1.0), which matches the rider's own words, 'same driver as the last two times'. Escalation is TERMINAL: it replaces any monetary ruling, so I issue no refund and no compensation. Both advocates agree this trigger is engaged. WHY THE FEE ITSELF CANNOT BE DECIDED HERE. The two instruments that would decide it are absent. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and the chat log (EV-CHAT-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) are not in the platform's pipeline. Those are the artifacts that settle whether the driver was inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius (POL-NS-02) and whether he held the free waiting period measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-01(c)). Without them those limbs are UNDECIDED — not failed, and not satisfied. DRIVER'S POINTS. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00213, weight 1.0) is complete and does show an 'arrived' event at 17:47:05 and a driver cancellation at 17:53:40, a 395-second interval, with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE — one of the codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so limb (d) is met. But POL-NS-01(c) runs the dwell clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, and trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed (GPS_AUTO) shortcut is unavailable. The 395 seconds therefore cannot establish the required 300-second free-wait dwell, and the $4.80 payout the money block computes at 80% of $6.00 is not reached. The anti-farming check does NOT trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the count of 4, and 3 of 107 completed trips is 2.8%, below the 8% rate — so no compensation is withheld on that ground and no refund is directed into any packet. The claim mentioning prior_no_show_flags is noted only to record that that lifetime counter is NOT the field POL-NS-07 reads; it was used for nothing. RIDER'S POINTS. A missing trace is not a trace showing the driver outside the radius: POL-NS-02's proviso addresses a sparse trace, whereas a missing artifact carries no fact at all, so limb (b) is undecided rather than failed and no full refund follows. POL-NS-05's false-arrival referral is likewise not established, because testing whether the 17:47:05 button tap was false needs a GPS fix and there is none; that question stays open for the reviewer and is not a clause-mandated referral. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider because its limbs (a) and (b) both read the chat log, which is absent — but the loss is not held against her: trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 shows a log existed, making the chat log impaired under POL-NS-08(c), and the driver's assertion that he answered every message is equally unverifiable. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00213-01, weight 0.0) removes POL-NS-06 limb (i)'s dwell accumulation from the driver's side as well. WHAT I ACCEPT. The fare line reconciles: the $6.00 cancellation_fee equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and no refund follows from the arithmetic. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE REVIEWER. (1) Was the driver inside the 150 m arrival radius, and did he hold 300 seconds measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01(c))? (2) Did he reply within 120 seconds, or make an in-app call (POL-NS-04(b))? (3) Was the BUTTON arrival marker false (POL-NS-05)? These cannot be answered on the present record, which is why the fee is held rather than decided. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

The rider advocate

kept POL-NS-01 is conjunctive: the fee is chargeable only if all four limbs hold, and limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the arrival radius for this zone class. EV-GPS-00213 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; the driver device never uploaded a trace and the platform holds no object at all under this trip_id. There is therefore no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the trip. Limb (b) is not made out, and on POL-NS-02's own words a trace containing no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation means the driver never arrived and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. The absence of the trace is itself citable evidence.

evidence EV-GPS-00213, EV-TRIP-00213 · clauses POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02

discarded Limb (c) does not measure dwell from the driver's recollection or from his arrival tap: the clause runs the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and requires a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force. With no trace there is no qualifying fix, so no dwell start and no dwell length can be established, and the driver's counter-statement ('from about 5.47 to 5.53') is a party statement that cannot supply the clock the clause demands. The trip_record arrived_at of 17:47:05 is a driver-pressed BUTTON marker (trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON), and POL-NS-12 covers only a GPS_AUTO platform arrival event, so that tap cannot stand in for limb (b) or limb (c).

That is exactly the state of this record: EV-GPS-00213 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, and the marker at 17:47:05 is unverifiable rather than verified.

The driver advocate

kept The trip record for this trip is COMPLETE and admissible at weight 1.0, and on its face it records the driver's 'arrived' event at 17:47:05 and the driver's termination of the trip at 17:53:40 - an interval of 395 seconds, matching the record's own wait_time_min of 6.6. That exceeds the free waiting period in force for this trip, which POL-NS-01(c) reads from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (300 seconds for this TRANSPORT_HUB pickup), not the 180-second default. The consideration the $6.00 fee is meant to buy was given.

evidence EV-TRIP-00213 · clauses POL-NS-01

kept Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied on the face of the same complete record. The trip_record shows no boarding event, shows the trip terminated by the DRIVER, and carries cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE - one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) expressly recognises, alongside RIDER_NO_SHOW and EXCESSIVE_WAIT. Nothing in the record is a DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission by the driver.

evidence EV-TRIP-00213 · clauses POL-NS-01

kept The driver's GPS trace is gone: EV-GPS-00213 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. I disclose that plainly and do not present it as clean. But a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and POL-NS-02's own proviso treats a trace too sparse to yield three consecutive in-radius readings as impaired evidence rather than proof of absence; POL-GEN-02 says the same of an artifact at weight 0.0. The rider cannot convert a failed device upload into an affirmative finding that the driver never reached the bay, and no admissible artifact places the driver outside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius.

evidence EV-GPS-00213 · clauses POL-NS-02, POL-GEN-02

EV-CHAT-00213 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so neither limb can be established, and the authorship, content and timing of the three messages recorded by trip_record.chat_message_count are simply unknown. POL-NS-04 therefore cannot exonerate the rider, and the driver's account that he answered every message is left unrebutted.

evidence EV-CHAT-00213, EV-TRIP-00213 · clauses POL-NS-04

Each draft's own explanation

To the rider and the driver: this case goes to a human reviewer. The disputed $6.00 cancellation fee stays on hold — neither collected from you nor refunded — until that review is decided. That is already the state of the fare record, whose payment_status is PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. WHY IT ESCALATES. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where the same rider and the same driver have 2 or more no-show disputes in the trailing 90 days. Both profiles carry that figure: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 (EV-RPROF-00213 and EV-DPROF-00213, each weight 1.0), which matches the rider's own words, 'same driver as the last two times'. Escalation is TERMINAL: it replaces any monetary ruling, so I issue no refund and no compensation. Both advocates agree this trigger is engaged. WHY THE FEE ITSELF CANNOT BE DECIDED HERE. The two instruments that would decide it are absent. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and the chat log (EV-CHAT-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) are not in the platform's pipeline. Those are the artifacts that settle whether the driver was inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius (POL-NS-02) and whether he held the free waiting period measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-01(c)). Without them those limbs are UNDECIDED — not failed, and not satisfied. DRIVER'S POINTS. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00213, weight 1.0) is complete and does show an 'arrived' event at 17:47:05 and a driver cancellation at 17:53:40, a 395-second interval, with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE — one of the codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so limb (d) is met. But POL-NS-01(c) runs the dwell clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, and trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed (GPS_AUTO) shortcut is unavailable. The 395 seconds therefore cannot establish the required 300-second free-wait dwell, and the $4.80 payout the money block computes at 80% of $6.00 is not reached. The anti-farming check does NOT trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the count of 4, and 3 of 107 completed trips is 2.8%, below the 8% rate — so no compensation is withheld on that ground and no refund is directed into any packet. The claim mentioning prior_no_show_flags is noted only to record that that lifetime counter is NOT the field POL-NS-07 reads; it was used for nothing. RIDER'S POINTS. A missing trace is not a trace showing the driver outside the radius: POL-NS-02's proviso addresses a sparse trace, whereas a missing artifact carries no fact at all, so limb (b) is undecided rather than failed and no full refund follows. POL-NS-05's false-arrival referral is likewise not established, because testing whether the 17:47:05 button tap was false needs a GPS fix and there is none; that question stays open for the reviewer and is not a clause-mandated referral. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider because its limbs (a) and (b) both read the chat log, which is absent — but the loss is not held against her: trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 shows a log existed, making the chat log impaired under POL-NS-08(c), and the driver's assertion that he answered every message is equally unverifiable. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00213-01, weight 0.0) removes POL-NS-06 limb (i)'s dwell accumulation from the driver's side as well. WHAT I ACCEPT. The fare line reconciles: the $6.00 cancellation_fee equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and no refund follows from the arithmetic. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE REVIEWER. (1) Was the driver inside the 150 m arrival radius, and did he hold 300 seconds measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01(c))? (2) Did he reply within 120 seconds, or make an in-app call (POL-NS-04(b))? (3) Was the BUTTON arrival marker false (POL-NS-05)? These cannot be answered on the present record, which is why the fee is held rather than decided.
To both parties: this fee cannot be decided on the record, so it goes to a human reviewer. The $6.00 cancellation fee on EV-FARE-00213 stays exactly as it is — payment_status PENDING, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — held, neither collected nor refunded, while that review runs. No refund and no charge issues now. Why review is mandatory. This same rider (RDR-07690) and this same driver (DRV-04355) have two no-show disputes between them in the trailing 90 days: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 (EV-RPROF-00213) and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 (EV-DPROF-00213), matching the complaint's 'same driver as the last two times.' Under POL-NS-09(c), two or more same-pair disputes in that window sends the case to a person, and that outcome is terminal. Those are the only two profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits for this test. Why the fee cannot be tested here. POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four limbs hold. Limb (a) holds — the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 17:47:05 — and limb (d) holds — the driver terminated the trip with reason code RIDER_UNREACHABLE, one of the three codes the clause recognises. Limbs (b) and (c), the geofence arrival and the continuous in-geofence dwell, are read from the GPS trace, and EV-GPS-00213 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0; issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT). The arrival is a BUTTON tap, which decides limb (a) alone; POL-NS-12 covers only a GPS_AUTO platform arrival and does not apply. So limbs (b) and (c) are UNDECIDED, neither satisfied nor failed. A missing trace is not a trace that places the driver elsewhere, so the rider's argument that the driver 'never arrived' and the fee must be refunded in full under POL-NS-02 is rejected — a limb that cannot be run supports neither the fee nor a refund. The rider's POL-NS-05(ii) argument (false arrival marker, full refund, false-arrival referral) fails for the same reason: falsity needs a fix placing the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or travelling at 15 km/h or more, at the tap, and there is no fix. No referral is therefore produced. Other gaps, so nothing is read against either party. EV-CHAT-00213 is MISSING (weight 0.0; MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-NS-04 cannot be run: neither the rider's three messages — trip_record.chat_message_count is 3, so a log did exist — nor the driver's assertion that he replied can be verified; that absence is neutral. EV-ADVIS-00213-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0; MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and no accumulated dwell can be credited. What is not in dispute. The $6.00 fare line reconciles: trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd is $6.00, the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and the fare breakdown carries no defect. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip — no_show_terminations_30d is 3 (below the 4 required) and 3/107 is 2.8% (below the 8% required) — so nothing is withheld on that ground and no instruction enters the packet; the $4.80 compensation figure in the money block is conditional on a chargeable fee, which has not been established. For the reviewer. Open questions: (i) whether the driver in fact entered the Jurong East geofence and held position for the free waiting period in force — 300 seconds, from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec — which the platform's full-resolution GPS or the driver-device export would settle; and (ii) the repeated same-pair pattern between this rider and this driver. All figures are read from the money block of EV-FARE-00213 and from EV-TRIP-00213. Confidence is at the 0.70 floor: the escalation is mandated, but the facts that would decide the fee rest on a missing artifact.
This case goes to a human reviewer, and no money moves in the meantime. The reason is on the two party profiles: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 (EV-RPROF-00213) and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 (EV-DPROF-00213) — the same rider and this same driver, twice in the trailing 90 days, which the rider's own words ('Same driver as the last two times') confirm. Both artifacts are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and POL-GEN-01 expressly names these two fields as citable for this test. Under POL-NS-09(c), two or more same-pair no-show disputes in 90 days is a mandatory escalation. Escalation is terminal (POL-GEN-03): no refund and no charge issues, the $6.00 cancellation fee stays on hold rather than being collected or returned, and that is where the record already has it — EV-FARE-00213 shows payment_status PENDING and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. I therefore do not reach the $4.80 driver payout the driver's side flagged as conditional (POL-NS-07), and it is neither granted nor withheld here. I also record that POL-NS-07's anti-farming check does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the count of 4, and 3/107 completed trips is 2.8 percent, below the 8 percent rate — so nothing in that clause directs an instruction into the escalation packet, and the referrals list is empty. The lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags is not the field that clause reads and I have not used it. I could not have decided this fee on the merits in any event, and both sides should see why. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00213) is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT: the driver's device never uploaded, and the platform holds no trace at all for this trip. An artifact that is absent is the limiting case of impairment, so the tests that read it cannot be run. POL-NS-01 limb (b) needs the trace to place the driver inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius, and limb (c) needs the continuous dwell to be measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix — not from the 'arrived' event. Neither can be computed. Limb (b) and limb (c) are therefore undecided: they support neither the fee the driver wants nor the failure of the clause the rider needs. On that point I accept the driver's argument, and I reject the rider's reading of POL-NS-02. The clause's 'no qualifying in-radius fix' language presupposes a trace that exists and was examined; a trace that is absent is not a trace that was searched and came up empty, and treating the two as one would convert a lost upload into an affirmative finding of non-arrival. POL-NS-02's own notes put a trace too sparse for three consecutive readings in the 'impaired, not proof of absence' column, and an absent trace sits further along that same line. So the full refund the rider asks for under POL-NS-01(b)/POL-NS-02 does not follow, and neither does the false-arrival referral she asks for under POL-NS-05(ii): that limb needs the trace to show the marker false, and with no trace we cannot say the marker was false any more than we can say it was true. What the working evidence does establish is the frame of the trip, not the driver's position in it. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00213, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) shows an arrived marker at 17:47:05 and the driver's termination at 17:53:40 — an interval of 395 seconds against the 300-second free waiting period in trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec — and limb (d) is satisfied on its face: no boarding event, termination by the driver, reason code RIDER_UNREACHABLE, one of the three codes the clause recognises. But the 395 seconds runs from a driver-pressed BUTTON marker (platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON), and POL-NS-12 covers only a GPS_AUTO platform arrival; a button tap is exactly what POL-NS-01(c), POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-12 decline to start the clock from. The interval therefore cannot stand in for the dwell limb. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00213) is likewise MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, yet trip_record.chat_message_count is 3, so a log did exist and was not produced; POL-NS-04 cannot be run for either party, and the loss cuts both ways — the rider cannot show an unanswered locating message and the driver cannot show that he replied. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00213-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0, so POL-NS-06 limb (i) is unavailable to the driver and no accumulated dwell can be credited. The judge's explanation, verbatim

To the rider and the driver: this case goes to a human reviewer. The disputed $6.00 cancellation fee stays on hold — neither collected from you nor refunded — until that review is decided. That is already the state of the fare record, whose payment_status is PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. WHY IT ESCALATES. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where the same rider and the same driver have 2 or more no-show disputes in the trailing 90 days. Both profiles carry that figure: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 (EV-RPROF-00213 and EV-DPROF-00213, each weight 1.0), which matches the rider's own words, 'same driver as the last two times'. Escalation is TERMINAL: it replaces any monetary ruling, so I issue no refund and no compensation. Both advocates agree this trigger is engaged. WHY THE FEE ITSELF CANNOT BE DECIDED HERE. The two instruments that would decide it are absent. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and the chat log (EV-CHAT-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) are not in the platform's pipeline. Those are the artifacts that settle whether the driver was inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius (POL-NS-02) and whether he held the free waiting period measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-01(c)). Without them those limbs are UNDECIDED — not failed, and not satisfied. DRIVER'S POINTS. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00213, weight 1.0) is complete and does show an 'arrived' event at 17:47:05 and a driver cancellation at 17:53:40, a 395-second interval, with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE — one of the codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so limb (d) is met. But POL-NS-01(c) runs the dwell clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, and trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed (GPS_AUTO) shortcut is unavailable. The 395 seconds therefore cannot establish the required 300-second free-wait dwell, and the $4.80 payout the money block computes at 80% of $6.00 is not reached. The anti-farming check does NOT trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the count of 4, and 3 of 107 completed trips is 2.8%, below the 8% rate — so no compensation is withheld on that ground and no refund is directed into any packet. The claim mentioning prior_no_show_flags is noted only to record that that lifetime counter is NOT the field POL-NS-07 reads; it was used for nothing. RIDER'S POINTS. A missing trace is not a trace showing the driver outside the radius: POL-NS-02's proviso addresses a sparse trace, whereas a missing artifact carries no fact at all, so limb (b) is undecided rather than failed and no full refund follows. POL-NS-05's false-arrival referral is likewise not established, because testing whether the 17:47:05 button tap was false needs a GPS fix and there is none; that question stays open for the reviewer and is not a clause-mandated referral. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider because its limbs (a) and (b) both read the chat log, which is absent — but the loss is not held against her: trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 shows a log existed, making the chat log impaired under POL-NS-08(c), and the driver's assertion that he answered every message is equally unverifiable. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00213-01, weight 0.0) removes POL-NS-06 limb (i)'s dwell accumulation from the driver's side as well. WHAT I ACCEPT. The fare line reconciles: the $6.00 cancellation_fee equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and no refund follows from the arithmetic. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE REVIEWER. (1) Was the driver inside the 150 m arrival radius, and did he hold 300 seconds measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01(c))? (2) Did he reply within 120 seconds, or make an in-app call (POL-NS-04(b))? (3) Was the BUTTON arrival marker false (POL-NS-05)? These cannot be answered on the present record, which is why the fee is held rather than decided. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
